MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 12, 2022
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Bucknum
at 5:00 p.m., on July 12, 2022, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on July 7, 2022, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Paragraph (1) of Subdivision (d) of
  Section 54956.9. Schlesinger v. City of Mission Viejo: 30-2022-01253878-CU-WM-CJC

Aaron Hand, M.V.: Outlined the Courts Preliminary Injunction and stressed that the Court stated
that the seats held by Trish Kelley and Brian Goodell will be up for election in November of 2022.
Criticized the City Council and City Attorney for the confusion regarding the upcoming election.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Criticized the City Council and City Attorney. Voice concerned that the City
Attorney has not kept the City Council updated. She questioned the City Attorney’s reasons for
leaving his previous law firms and raised suspicion on the reasons. She stated the State Attorney

City Council Minutes  1  July 12, 2022
 and the Former Chair of the Senate Elections Committee are raising concerns about you staying in
your seats beyond your two-year elected term. The time has come to allow the citizens of our city
to have the right for staggered terms which is part of our election history and heritage.

The City Attorney clarified that a preliminary injunction is an order prohibiting an action to preserve
the status quo while the underlying court case is decided. The underlying court case is the writ
action which has a Demurrer set in September but that will probably shift because there was an
amended complaint trying to fix the problems in the first one.
He noted that the court only issued a preliminary injunction that will be upon final adjudication
perhaps changed.

CS2. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:06 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced there were two Closed Session items. CS1 will be reported
out in junction with Item 20 this evening and CS2 there was no reportable action.

INVOCATION: Mayor Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize K-9 Keto and his Handler Deputy Craig Sanders for Assisting in the
  Apprehension of a Perpetrator in a Stolen Vehicle

  Received presentation.

P2. Recognize Mission Viejo High School Swimmer Alexis Unter for Being was Selected to
  the USA Down Syndrome Swimming (USADSS) National Team, and Coach T. Sorenson
  for Being Selected as an Assistant Coach of the USADSS National Team this October in
  in Albufeira, Portugal

  Mayor Bucknum presented certificates.

P3. Friends of the Library Donation Presentation

  Received presentation.

PUBLIC COMMENTS
City Council Minutes  2  July 12, 2022
 Frank Fabrega, Rancho Mission Viejo: Thanked the City Council for their support in the success
of the Relay for Life that was held in June in which over $109,000 was raised. Over the past 28
years he stated that Relay for Life has raised over four million dollars for the American Cancer
Society.

Joshua Vecchione, M.V.: He asked the City Council to consider the Stein Mart Building to be used
as a Black Box Theater for the community.

Chad Halliburton, M.V.: Stated that Oakhouse Church is still interested in leasing the Stein Mart
Building even though the Planning Commission tabled at their meeting last night.

Tracy VanEvery, Lake Forest: Stated that she is very interested in the leasing of the Stein Mart
Building for Oakhouse Church for temporary use for one day of the week.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: He said at the Planning Commission last evening the discussion of the Stein
Mart Building renting to OakHouse Church was poorly presented. Questioned how the City Council
was going to see the Minutes from the last night’s Planning Commission Meeting.

Bob Ruesch, M.V.: Announced that he is running for City Council in District 1.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Discussed and recapped the June 28 ruling by Judge Shwarm. States that the
City continues to mislead and confuse the public about Judge Shwarm’s decision.

Aaron Hand, M.V.: He clarified that the court issued an order that all five seats are up for re-
election. He encouraged that the City Council to read the complaint and the amended complaint.

Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Spoke out on the mass shootings throughout our Country. Stated that
Congress passed gun law legislation with money coming from Congress for school security. Lastly,
he spoke out against Assembly Bill 2011.

Karee Delsigne, M.V.: Spoke on how much she loves the City and to be aware of the State pushing
for high-density living and our City needs to fight this to keep our conservative City.

Gabriel El Mahrek, M.V.: Spoke about his conviction against Pride Month and how he was called
a Nazi will protesting. He believes modern war is evil because it leads to death and suffering of
civilians.

Maria Lucia Gomez-Greenberg, M.V.: Spoke out against Council terms of four and six years. Stated
that residents deserve transparent and legal election process.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Commented on the 2007 Urban Land Institute report on the Village Center.
Pointed out that it was called a Specific Plan and asks that the Council to push for the development
of specific plan at the Village Center.

City Council Minutes  3  July 12, 2022
 Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Criticized the City Attorney of attacking speakers on their opinions and
beliefs. She accused the City Council of deception and protecting their seats and not allowing the
public to weigh in on the terms of the City Council.

Sabrina Phillips, M.V.: Introduced herself as the owner of Designing Women of Orange County an
interior design firm and pointed out the services her company provides.

Lynn Holmes, M.V.: Stated that trusting a City Council is critical and feels that the communication
from the City Council is inadequate and minimal. Criticized the City Attorney on confusing the
public.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 9, 12, 13, and 14 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the Consent
Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of June 28, 2022, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated June 17, 2022 in the Amount of $607,861.51

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated June 24, 2022 in the Amount of $1,210,914.28

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated July 1, 2022 in the Amount of $1,424,348.19

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for May 2022

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  4  July 12, 2022
 6.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for May 2022

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for May 2022

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for May 2022

  Received and filed.

10. Approval of Phase II Collaborative Design Team for Design Development - Core Area
  Vision Plan

  (1) Awarded a contract to Lab-Co (A22-27) in an amount not to exceed $43,000; (2) awarded
  a contract to Studio-111 (A22-28) in an amount not to exceed $129,870; and (3) issue a
  Purchase Order to RJM Design Group in an amount not to exceed $299,700.

11. 2022 Residential Resurfacing-Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 23838)

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to All American Asphalt, Inc.
  (A22-30) in the amount of $2,542,229.

15. Local Hazard Mitigation Plan Update

  (1) Approved the agreement for consulting services with Atlas Planning Solutions (A22-33)

  and (2) adopted Resolution 22-26 Amending the Fiscal Year 2022-23 Emergency

City Council Minutes  5  July 12, 2022
 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

9.  La Paz Bridge Rehabilitation and Road Widening Improvements (CIP 01756)

Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

Motion made by Council Member Raths, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) rescind the
award of construction contract of December 14, 2021 to Security Paving Company, Inc.; (2) award
the construction contract for the subject project to Flatiron West, Inc. in the amount of $15,465,786;
and (3) adopted Resolution 22-25 Amending the Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Budget for Costs Related
to Capital Improvement Project CIP 01756.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

12. License Agreement from September 2022 through December 2023 with OAKHOUSE
  CHURCH INC. to lease space at 25282 Marguerite Parkway

Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated she was not opposed to the temporary use of the building to the
Church, but to the process and lack of transparency and that the Vision Plan is not what residents
expected. She blames staff for putting the church in an awkward position and questioned why the
space was to be rented out without City Council authority.

Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to defer this item until
there is a recommendation from the Planning Commission.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

13. Memorandum of Understanding Between City of Mission Viejo and Pacific Symphony

Director of Library & Cultural Services Genesis Hansen presented the staff report.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to amend the
Memorandum of Understanding between City of Mission Viejo and Pacific Symphony (A22-32)
to provide the annual Symphony in the Cities concert plus additional programming for a cost not to
exceed $85,000 in FY 22/23 and come back at another time to amend for another $15,000 once we
have identified what that use is to be for.

City Council Minutes  6  July 12, 2022
 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

14. Annual Review of Residential and Commercial Integrated Waste Management Rates

Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to receive and file
the report.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

18. Oso Creek Golf Course Green Fee Rates Update

Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

Tim Lane, M.V.: Stated he understands the fee increase and suggested that there be an Oso Creek
Golf Club for $20 per month and get to have the resident fee. He gave kudos to the staff and
thanked staff for all the hard work keeping the course up.

Rick Sandzimier, M.V.: Complained that there was an error in the notice at the golf course that it
was incorrect which is why at the last meeting there was no one in attendance to speak on the item.
He also stated that when he reached out to staff and candidly the response was not professional and
that he did reach out to the four Council Members and were very responsive. Stated that the staff at
Oso Creek is great and pleasant to work with.

By consensus the City Council received the report.

NEW BUSINESS

19. Request of Four Homeowners Association Board of Directors to Manage Pest Control
  by All Authorized Means, Including Firearms

Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

The following spoke in favor of the recommended action: Ray Imatani, M.V.; Jon Goettsch, M.V.;
Michael Schlesinger, M.V.; and Elizabeth Mead, M.V.

City Council Minutes  7  July 12, 2022
 Art Levine, M.V.: Spoke against the recommended action. Stated that the Palmia Board was split
on this issue and implored the Council to not approve the variance.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to (1) approve the
request of Casta Del Sol Homeowners Association for a variance that will allow the association to
manage on-site nuisance wildlife by the most humane means possible for the health, safety and
welfare of the community; (2) approve the request of Mission Viejo Environmental Association for
a variance that will allow the association to manage on-site nuisance wildlife by the most humane
means possible for the health, safety and welfare of the community; (3) approve the request of
Palmia Masters Association for a variance that will allow the association to manage on-site nuisance
wildlife by the most humane means possible for the health, safety and welfare of the community;
and (4) approve an extension to the approved variance in effect for Tres Vistas Association that will
allow the association to manage on-site nuisance wildlife by the most humane means possible for
the health, safety and welfare of the community.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Sachs
NOES:  Raths
ABSENT:  None

20. Calling for a General Municipal Election on November 8, 2022 to Elect Five Members
  to the City Council for Districts 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5

City Clerk Kimberly Schmitt presented the staff report.

City Attorney Curly reported that the City’s recent Ordinance that established the election cycles
and districts. Firstly, we have been following our Municipal Code Section 2.04.140 that requires
four-year terms which is being done for all five districts. The second part the City is looking at
code modifications to re-establish the staggering of terms pursuant to the rule of law by ordinance.
He stated that it is very typical of an out-going Council to leave significant law term City matters
to the incoming Council. We will follow all five for four year-terms pursuant to the code and put
together options for ordinance amendments to re-start staggering and that will be done under the
control of the newly elected Council.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Pointed out that Resolution 18-52 was passed calling for a term of two years
for Greg, Ed and Wendy. He hopes that the Council will agree to stagger by having the top three
get four-year terms and the bottom two will be for two-year terms. He criticized the City Council
for allowing the City Attorney to brow beat the public speakers.

Michael Schlesinger, M.V.: Asked if the City Attorney will strike the demurrer. Quoted
Representative Murphy closing statement at the January 6 Hearing. He stressed that he wants free
and fair elections and accused the City Council of flagrantly resisted his efforts in obtaining the
Constitutional right to vote, including bringing a slap suit against him. He suggested staggered
terms to follow the Government Code 57377 by choosing four and two-year terms by lot.

City Council Minutes  8  July 12, 2022
 Jon Miller, M.V.: Stated in his opinion staggering terms is not an urgent issue. He agreed to run
all five district for four years. He suggested that we can get citizen process to determine how we
want to be represented and to put this to the voters in 2024 to be implemented in 2026

Elizabeth Mead, M.V.: Expressed her confusion over this issue over districts and staggered terms.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Quoted from the California Supreme Court Standard for Government
Attorneys. She accused the City Attorney of trying to keep the public off balance and word games
and to chill public participation. She stated that the right belongs to the public to decide how we
want to elect the City Council.

City Attorney Bill Curley read into record the language for Resolution 22-27 SECTION 1. That
pursuant to the requirements of the laws of the State of California relating to General Law Cities,
there is called and ordered to be held in the City of Mission Viejo, California, on Tuesday,
November 8, 2022, a General Municipal Election for the purpose of electing five (5) council
members for the full term of four years for all five (5) electoral districts (1, 2, 3, 4 & 5). This will
become if it is adopted your formal action for the reasons as mentioned.

Mayor Bucknum announced that given the impending election and lack of clarity the
implementation of the system she believes the City must take action for the purpose of good
governance and she recommended that the City Council proactively establish the voting process
pursuant to the City’s Municipal Code. By establishing that all five newly created City Council
Districts will be up for election for terms of four years each which would prevent significant
confusion and uncertainty heading into the General Election, particularly for voters and potential
candidates.

Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) adopt the amended
Resolution 22-27 Calling for the Holding of a General Municipal Election to be Held on Tuesday,
November 8, 2022, for the Election of Certain Officers as Required by the Provisions of the Laws
of the State of California Relating to General Law Cities; (2) adopt Resolution 22-28 Requesting
the Board of Supervisors of the County of Orange to Consolidate a General Municipal Election to
be Held on November 8, 2022, with the Statewide General Election to be Held on the Same Date
pursuant to § 10403 of the Elections Code; (3) adopt Resolution 22-29 Adopting Regulations for
Candidates for Elective Officer Pertaining to Candidate Statements Submitted to the Voters at an
Election to be Held on November 8, 2022; and (4) direct the City Clerk to schedule the adoption of
the resolution citing the election results and administration of the oath to the newly elected Council
Members on December 13, 2022, or as soon as possible thereafter.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

City Council Minutes  9  July 12, 2022
 21. Voting Delegate and Alternate(s) for the 2022 League of California Cities Annual
  Conference

Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to appoint Mayor Pro
Tem Sachs as voting delegate and Council Member Raths and Council Member Kelley as alternates
for the League of California Cities Conference Annual Business Meeting on Friday September 9,
2022.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

22. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

Assistant City Attorney Keith Rattay reminded everyone that the Symphony is on August 13.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

23. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell announced that he attended the Planning Commission Meeting last night
regarding the Oakhouse Church item and felt that the commissioners didn’t know what was going
on and felt that there was a feeling in the community that this came up rather quickly and lot of
people didn’t understand as well as some of the property owners in the Village Center. He stated
we can do a better job of communicating and he reiterated that there needs to be a better system to
communicate with the property owners in the Village Center. He felt that if we were going to make
the building available for people to use we should have had a fair process. Questioned if the Council
needs to give direction to the Planning Commission and would like it to be on the agenda for August
23.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley commended the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for the Fourth of July
Street Faire. She attended the SCORE Appreciation Event on July 5, SCORE is our group of senior
City Council Minutes  10  July 12, 2022
 citizens that assist Mission Viejo Police Services. Council Member Kelley also thanked the Mission
Viejo Friends of the Arts for putting up “pop-up art” events in various place around the City. She
attended the July 9 event at the Mission Viejo Dog Park. She outlined upcoming events: July 15
Concert on the Green with the band Family Style, July 16 Potocki Center will host a Steely Band
tribute band concert, July 20 Shakespeare by the Sea will be performing Romeo and Juliet at Oso
Viejo Park – Village Green, July 30 the Character Committee will be putting on a program called
The Road Map to Success at the Murray Center for all incoming high school students and their
parents, August 2 will be National Night Out at Flo Jo Park, and August 13 the Pacific Symphony
will be performing at Oso Viejo Park. Lastly, she announced that school starts August 15 for
Saddleback Valley School District, and August 16 for Capistrano Valley Unified School District.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths stated that we need to be more deliberative on our approach regarding the
Core Vision Plan and Stein Mart Building and asked staff to provide quarterly updates on the
status. He attended the July Fourth Street Faire and had a great time.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs stated that he along with the City Manager and City Attorney met with the
Local Government and Community Liaison Jesus Torres for the California Public Utilities
Commission (CPUC) regarding the mixed messages we receive on energy efficiency, time of use,
flex alert information from various State agencies. He stated that Mr. Torres related that one can
find the energy use and efficiency resources at www.energyupgradeca.org. The second issue dealt
with public safety power shut-offs, and the City Manager asked why are areas of the City or State
advised that power will be shut off when those power lines are underground. Thirdly, they discussed
the street light amortization billing and Mr. Torres will look to see if there is a regulatory remedy
to be notified once the payment schedule ends. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs commented on public speaker
Mr. Pianelli’s comments regarding mass shootings and stated he was in favor of his overall all
compassion on this subject but clarified that according to the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
a mass shooting is when three or more people are shot. He stated that over 60 to 62% of all firearm
shootings are suicides and unfortunately 18 to 26 daily suicides are coming from our Veteran
Community. Commented that in Chicago over the Fourth of July weekend there were 91 shootings
resulting in 19 deaths. He stated he is aggravated at the District Attorney’s that will take anyone
that is charged with a gun crime and they will take those gun crimes off the table when dealing with
plea bargains. These charges should remain, prosecution should take place and punish those who
disregard those laws. He stated that he also believes that they should all come to special
circumstances if a gun is used in a crime for anything. Mayor Pro Tem announced that Secure O.C.
Schools had a very successful meeting with the Orange County Archdiocese and we look forward
to moving forward with them and their security issues. Lastly, he stressed that we need to continue
to move forward with the Core Vision Plan and other items within the City.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum asked staff to keep updates regarding the Core Area and the Church lease at the
Stein Mart Building. She announced that at the free community concerts tables can be purchased
for $150 online. Mayor Bucknum also announced that there will be a Night Market the third
City Council Minutes  11  July 12, 2022
 Saturday of every month. Asked staff if printed maps can be made available at community events.
Mayor Bucknum spoke about Sober Living Homes and the status of an upcoming workshop which
will be either Monday August 1 or Wednesday August 3. Lastly, she said she hopes we can move
forward in the spirit of keeping the confusion to a minimum for our residents.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:04 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, August 23, 2022, at 5:00 p.m.
